statements.text: A fair basis is books per seller: Counter A averages $9$ and Counter B averages $6$.
Comparing totals alone is unfair here because the counters have different numbers of sellers.
Counter B is ahead on a fair typical basis because its total $54$ is larger than $27$.

stem: Neha compares two shop counters. Counter A has $3$ sellers and sold $27$ books in all. Counter B has $9$ sellers and sold $54$ books in all. She wants a fair comparison of typical sales when the counters have different sizes.

teacher.key_rationale: Per-seller averages (9 vs 6) fairly compare unequal group sizes; totals alone favour the larger staff. Statement 3 wrongly treats the larger total as the fair typical basis. Key is 1 and 2 only.
